title: When Youth Enter The Chat: An Epistemic Shift in the Validation of LLM-Based Measures of Student Talk
abstract: arXiv:2608.23780v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLMs are being used increasingly to measure aspects of student discourse (e.g. talk moves, collaboration, equity of voice) at scale. Typically, LLM-based measures of student talk use transcriptions of classroom conversations that only include verbal contributions, which de-contextualize student language. Common practices for validating these measures include comparing outputs against expert annotations by adults, using held out evaluation sets and F1 scores. We argue that these approaches are insufficient to ensure that such measures are meaningful and equitable for teaching and learning, particularly for racially and linguistically marginalized youth. In order to center the youth whose talk is being analyzed, re-contextualizing these classroom conversations and engaging youth in the research process is necessary. translated_title: 当青年进入对话：基于LLM的学生谈话测量验证中的认知转变
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.23780v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：大型语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被用于大规模测量学生话语的各个方面（例如，谈话动作、协作、声音公平性）。通常，基于LLM的学生谈话测量使用仅包含口头贡献的课堂对话转录，这使学生的语言脱离上下文。验证这些测量的常见实践包括将输出与成人的专家注释进行比较，使用留出评估集和F1分数。我们认为，这些方法不足以确保这些测量对教学和学习具有意义和公平性，特别是对于种族和语言边缘化的青年。为了以被分析谈话的青年为中心，需要重新情境化这些课堂对话，并让青年参与研究过程。与青年共享认知权威，最终以他们的视角为中心，并为分析增添关键细微差别。
tldr: 本文提出，验证基于LLM的学生谈话测量时，应通过重新情境化对话和让青年参与研究来共享认知权威，以确保测量对边缘化青年有意义且公平。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that validating LLM-based measures of student talk should involve re-contextualizing conversations and engaging youth in research to share epistemic authority, ensuring measures are meaningful and equitable for marginalized youth.
